records.research_claim: Store 29 June 1613 as a Julian day-level event so a future date-aware renderer can keep the theatre before the fire.

records.name: Indicative English woodland cover
records.methodology: Broad historical synthesis; archaeological/documentary estimates with changing definitions, not a complete annual series or Welsh estimate.

records.basis: Broad Roman-period endpoint band; source does not date individual changes.
Approximate late-eleventh-century woodland plus wood pasture, indexed at Domesday year.
About 10 percent by the fourteenth century; no exact year supplied.

records.app_claim: National rendering uses 20% at 400, 25% at 600, 15% at 1086 and 8% at 1350, with an explicit modelling note.
records.research_claim: Current official synthesis gives little overall Roman-to-early-medieval change, about 15% late-eleventh-century woodland/wood pasture and about 10% by the fourteenth century. Keep the app curve explicitly illustrative; this is an alternative synthesis, not a measured replacement.

records.name: London Black Death mortality synthesis
records.methodology: Museum estimate from archaeology, wills and descriptions; no contemporary central death register.

records.basis: Museum synthesis, not a counted death register.

records.app_claim: London event note gives November 1348 to 1349–50.

records.name: London major plague mortality fractions
records.methodology: Introductory historical synthesis gives 20–25 percent for major outbreaks; this range is not an independently measured confidence interval.

records.app_claim: London timeline ends with James I’s death; it has no separate 1563, 1603 or 1625 plague events.
records.research_claim: These three major plague outbreaks are identified by Boulton; they belong in the event layer, with the 1625 outbreak distinct from the king’s death.

records.value_text: Bills covered the City and liberties through 1603; out-parishes entered in 1604. Raw totals across that boundary are not directly comparable.
